title: Start, stop and restart an animation
source: A3 Q1 · animation task
requirements: Use the practice student number 2026001. Create a web page that initially displays 1 + 2026001 = 2026002. Use inline CSS to make the equation red and 60px.
Display two clickable texts: "Start Animation" in orange and "Stop Animation" in purple.

When the user clicks Start Animation, update the equation every second. After one second, display 3 + 2026001 = 2026004. After another second, display 5 + 2026001 = 2026006. Continue with 7, 9, and so on.
When the user clicks Stop Animation, stop the updates and display the original equation: 1 + 2026001 = 2026002.
If the user clicks Start Animation again, start the sequence again with 3 after one second, then 5, 7, and so on.
checks: The first update occurs one second after Start, and the following updates are one second apart.
Stop restores the initial equation immediately. A later Start begins again at 3, rather than continuing the stopped value.
adaptation: The assignment requires the learner’s own student number. This public practice uses a fixed sample identity. The reference also prevents duplicate timers; that lab robustness detail is not a new assignment marking item.

source: FormValidation lecture pp. 4–6, 8–22; Week 13: onsubmit return; L05 task form
